title: First morning. Monsoon Malabar. Nothing added.
body: Made the Moka pot in near-darkness. The smell arrived before I was ready for it — earthy, something almost medicinal. Tobacco-adjacent. I had not expected coffee to smell like a forest floor at this hour. Drank it standing at the kitchen window. The sky was still completely dark. I am not sure what I was expecting to feel.
observations: Brew time roughly 4 min — did not time it properly
Water was probably too hot, forgot to let it rest
Taste: heavy, long finish, low acidity
note: Monsoon Malabar felt emotionally heavier at 5AM. Not bad. Just heavy.

title: L-theanine, first try. The edge went somewhere.
body: Same beans. Added 200mg L-theanine dissolved in a small amount of hot water, then poured the coffee over it. I did not notice anything for the first 20 minutes. Then around 5:05 I realised I had been reading the same paragraph three times — not because I could not understand it, but because I wanted to. That is different from my usual morning. The caffeine was still there. It just had fewer corners.
observations: L-theanine: 200mg, NOW Foods capsule opened into cup
Dissolved in 2 tbsp water before adding coffee
Taste: no real change — maybe slightly sweeter perception
note: L-theanine softened the caffeine edge noticeably. I stopped noticing the room for a while.

title: Ashwagandha alone. Isolating the signal.
body: Swallowed the KSM-66 capsule immediately on waking, with a full glass of water. No theanine today — I wanted to know what ashwagandha alone does. The coffee was the same. Around 5:15 something in my chest was quieter. I cannot describe it better than that. The low-level background pressure of the morning — the awareness of the ticking clock, the hour I needed to protect — had been turned down. Not off. Just down.
observations: KSM-66 600mg: Carbamide Forte, taken dry on waking
First noticed effect at roughly 45 minutes
note: Background noise in my chest turned a notch down. The work felt less pressured.

title: Too much cacao. A lesson in restraint.
body: Added 3g of raw cacao to the grounds. A mistake I will not repeat. The bitterness did not stack — it multiplied. By 5:30 I had a low headache starting behind my eyes and the focus session was gone. I spent the time drinking water and reading nothing in particular. I wrote one sentence and deleted it. The cacao was not the only problem — I think the grind was also too fine and the extraction went long. Everything that can go wrong did.
observations: Raw cacao: 3g directly in Moka pot grounds — too much
note: 1g is the ceiling. This one belongs in the failed column.

title: Full morning protocol. Something changed.
body: Ashwagandha on waking. Then: Blue Tokai instant, L-theanine, 1g cacao, a pinch each of cardamom and cinnamon. First time making it as a sachet — everything pre-measured the night before, just dissolve and go. It took 90 seconds to make. I sat down at 4:35. At 5:10 I noticed I had been writing for 35 minutes without checking my phone. I did not plan to do that. It just happened. That is the signal I was looking for. This is the first cup that felt quieter than my thoughts.
note: 35 minutes without checking my phone. That is the data point I needed.

title: Rhodiola at 11am. The fog thinned.
body: The usual mid-morning depletion had arrived. The kind where sentences feel longer than they should and small decisions take more thought than they deserve. Made a reduced-caffeine cup — Blue Tokai instant, 2g, with rhodiola 400mg and cinnamon. I did not expect much. By 11:45 the quality of my thinking had changed. It was not a stimulant feeling. More like the fog had thinned. I could see further into the problem I was working on. I am not sure I would have noticed it if I had not been logging.
note: Not stimulated. Clarified. The fog thinned. Different from caffeine.

title: Evening cup — decaf, reishi, warm milk. The house was quiet.
body: Swiss Water decaf from Blue Tokai. Reishi 500mg. Ashwagandha 300mg. A small amount of cacao, cardamom, vanilla. Warm whole milk, not boiling. My daughter had been asleep for an hour. The sitting was as much the point as the drinking. This was the first time coffee felt like it was winding me down rather than winding me up. The bitterness felt useful today. Sleep quality the next morning was the best of the week.
observations: Sleep the following night: noticeably deeper
note: The cup matched the silence. Sleep quality: best of the week.

title: Social formula — cacao, rose, cardamom, cold.
body: First attempt at a recipe for when guests are there. Dark roast Blue Tokai instant, cacao, cardamom, rose water powder, a small amount of coconut sugar. Cold water, ice. Served in a small glass. My wife tasted it without being told what was in it. She asked if it was from a café. That is probably the most useful piece of feedback I have received so far. I placed one cardamom pod on top of the glass. It looked intentional.
observations: Coconut sugar: 1g — makes the rose come forward
note: She asked if it was from a café. The experiment worked.
